hints.title: This is a component count
hints.body: A cluster is exactly a connected component of an undirected graph. What does one traversal discover starting from an unvisited computer?

hints.title: Explore each unvisited computer
hints.body: Keep a visited array. Each time you find an unvisited computer, increment the cluster count and explore every computer reachable from it.

hints.title: Use the matrix as the adjacency list
hints.body: From computer `i`, every column `j` with `connected[i][j] == 1` is a neighbor. A stack or a queue works; mark a computer when you add it so it is not explored twice.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
visited = array of false of length n
clusters = 0
for start from 0 to n - 1:
    if visited[start]: continue
    clusters += 1
    stack = [start]
    visited[start] = true
    while stack is not empty:
        node = stack.pop()
        for neighbor from 0 to n - 1:
            if connected[node][neighbor] == 1 and not visited[neighbor]:
                visited[neighbor] = true
                stack.push(neighbor)
return clusters
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution. Marking on push prevents duplicate work.
